title: I made a Three.js dinosaur survival game (3x3km island) with opus 5.5 in 22 days. Here's what worked and where I struggled (free to play in browser)
author: ibuildtools

**▶ Play it free in your browser - not Safari or mobile (yet) :D @** [**feralbloodline.com**](https://feralbloodline.com/)

Feral Bloodline is a Three.js survival game where you live one creature’s whole life on a prehistoric island: hatch, eat, stay alive, find a nest. Your young inherit adaptations based on how you played, so the real goal is keeping your bloodline going across generations.

**How I built it**

I used Claude Code with Opus 5.5 and didn’t write a single line of code by hand.

* **Time:** 22 days (Oct 29 to Nov 19), and I worked on it 19 of them
* **Repo:** 160 commits, about 47k lines of TypeScript on Three.js, 584 automated tests
* **Usage:** about 2 billion tokens, roughly $810 at API list prices (mostly cached context being re-read)

My role consisted of playing every build and writing up what was wrong, usually 10 to 20 things per round, with screenshots and fps numbers. Then I sent it back and played the next build.

I also made sure to make every single design call. example: for smarter herds I decided how exactly they should behave: they sense you by sight, sound and scent on the wind, they stampede and then stay wary, and the adults defend the young.

Partway through I set up the Claude Code Game Studios agent framework and gave it a few standing rules: commit and push on its own, but stop and ask me before any change that could lose player saves.

**What worked well**

Performance surprised me most. An early version ran at 8 to 14 fps on my machine. I pushed for real measurements instead of guesses, so it built a profiler, found what was eating GPU time, batched props, added LODs and used mist to cap view distance. Same scenes went to 26 to 53 fps.

Once I’d settled how species and inheritance should work, it scaled the game from 3 species to 20, with 136 adaptations your offspring can inherit. Kills leave carcasses that fall or sink, your young inherit a faint map showing where ancestors were attacked and where their bones are, crocs leave the water to hunt, and pterosaurs snatch prey from the air.

I also built stuff I’d never have bothered with on my own: an admin dashboard with a live globe of who’s playing, and in-game messaging so I can reply to feedback without email.

**Where I struggled**

Creature models are my biggest time sink. I’ve spent hours on Sketchfab and elsewhere looking for free high-poly dinosaurs that are rigged, animated and free to use with attribution, and most aren’t all three. When I find one with no skeleton, I have Claude write Blender scripts to rig and animate it, then I check every gait in-game myself, because a bad walk cycle ruins everything.

Feel was the other one. I wanted a realistic hit effect splattering the camera lens, and it took five rounds of play, screenshot, explain, retry, all in one day. Every version was technically “done” and still looked wrong. What finally worked was my idea: recolor the raindrops-on-lens effect, which already looked great.

And Claude can’t play the game, so the bugs were on me to find: a wound effect that ballooned into a body-sized blob, herds spinning at the water’s edge, my body floating in mid-air after I died of my wounds. Each was a quick fix once I described it, but finding them took hours of play. Same with sound. It can’t hear anything, so I tuned the audio by ear: footsteps that change with the ground, bites you can actually hear, a menu soundscape that doesn’t get old.

**What’s next**

* Better visuals throughout, including high-poly animal models
* Better sound
* Optimization for low-RAM devices, to get ready for mobile if there’s interest
* Multiplayer

Try it and tell me what breaks: [feralbloodline.com](https://feralbloodline.com/). There’s a feedback button in the game, I read everything, and I can reply to you right in the game.

Anyone found a good source for rigged, animated creature models that are free to use? That’s been my biggest bottleneck. Looking forward to your thoughts!
